title: So Fades the Lovely, Blooming Flower
description: So Fades the Lovely, Blooming Flower in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 583 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: So fades the love-ly, bloom-ing flower, Frail, smil-ing so-lace of an hour; So soon our tran-sient com-forts fly, And plea-sure on-ly blooms to die.

lines: So fades the lovely, blooming flower,
Frail, smiling solace of an hour;
So soon our transient comforts fly,
And pleasure only blooms to die.
Is there no kind, no healing art,
To soothe the anguish of the heart?
Spirit of grace, be ever nigh:
Thy comforts are not made to die.
Let gentle patience smile on pain,
Hope wipes the tear from sorrow's eye,
And faith points upward to the sky.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
